headline: $352M Bitget hack contained; BTC holds $84,000 as the bond selloff pauses
summary: At 13:37 UTC on 25 September BTC is $84,081.80 against an $84,380.00 open (-0.35%), ETH $2,700.53 against $2,687.22 (+0.50%) and SOL $119.86 against $117.02 (+2.43%), with all three still up 8.3%, 8.7% and 14.2% on the week - so today is consolidation under $85,000, not a dip. The one acute event is an exchange breach: Bitget lost $351.6m in unauthorized transfers starting 18:31 UTC on 24 September, blames spoofed transfer data pushed through its own authorization system rather than stolen private keys, points at North Korea on VPN and IP evidence, and still has withdrawals suspended while deposits and trading run - the loss is covered by a User Protection Fund that held over $464m, and BGB is only 3-5% below pre-hack levels, which is why this has not become a market event. The macro backdrop actually improved overnight: the 10-year Treasury yield eased 7bp to 5.171% after jumping more than 20bp over the prior two sessions to its highest since 2007, the dollar index slipped below 101, and Brent fell about 1% to roughly $105. Underneath, the bid is real and the leverage is not: US spot bitcoin ETFs took $191m on Thursday for a sixth straight day and $2.8bn over the streak, while Hyperliquid open interest has fallen to $3.39bn on BTC, $2.96bn on ETH and $726m on SOL from $4.02bn, $3.18bn and $746m on 22 September, with funding flat at 0.00125%/h on all three. Fear & Greed is 71 and the composite reads 64.3, both Greed, but 24-hour news tone is negative at -0.56 - a market that is positioned lightly, paid for by spot flow, sitting on top of one unresolved custody story.

BTC.note: $84,081.80, 0.35% under the open and 39% up an $83,348.90-$85,247.40 band after the year's largest options expiry cleared at 08:00 UTC, with funding flat at 0.00125%/h, the premium thin at 0.019% and Hyperliquid open interest down to $3.39bn from $4.02bn on 22 September - the tape has been de-levered into strength rather than crowded long.

ETH.note: $2,700.53, up 0.50% and sitting 57% up its $2,645.35-$2,742.42 range with open interest at $2.96bn against $3.18bn three days ago, but the futures premium is the richest of the three at 0.084%, so ETH is where the remaining speculative lean sits.

SOL.note: $119.86, up 2.43% and the closest of the three to its day high in a $114.10-$122.20 range, the week's leader at +14.2% and part of a broad altcoin bid (XRP +5.5%, QNT +39%, ONDO +27%), on the thinnest book at $726m of open interest - which makes it the most reflexive in both directions.

drivers.title: Bitget loses $351.6m in the largest exchange breach of 2026, withdrawals still frozen
drivers.detail: Bitget detected unauthorized transfers from parts of its hot and warm wallet infrastructure at 18:31 UTC on 24 September totalling about $351.6m. Its CEO says attackers compromised a backend wallet system and fabricated transfer data so that Bitget's own authorization process moved the funds, rather than stealing private keys, and that VPN and IP evidence with a prior history of North Korean activity points at Lazarus. Withdrawals remain suspended while deposits and trading continue; the loss is inside a User Protection Fund that held more than $464m - roughly 76% of it - and the exchange claims over $1bn of proprietary assets backing users 1:1. The market has taken it as contained: BGB is only 3-5% below pre-hack levels and BTC is flat. The open risk is the withdrawal freeze itself, with an incident report due by 21:30 UTC today.

drivers.title: The bond selloff pauses: 10-year yield eases to 5.171% from 2007 highs
drivers.detail: The US 10-year Treasury yield slipped 7bp to 5.171% after jumping more than 20bp across the previous two sessions, including an 18bp move on Wednesday that took it to its highest level since 2007 and dragged BTC from about $87,200 to $83,500. The dollar index is below 101, the yen is up 0.6% at 158 for its best day in more than two weeks, gold is above $4,300 and Brent is about 1% lower near $105 on reports of a phased US-Iran deal. This is the single biggest reason today is quiet rather than ugly - and the reason it can turn again, since nothing about the yield level has been resolved, only its rate of change.

drivers.title: Spot bitcoin ETFs buy through the yield shock: six straight days, $2.8bn
drivers.detail: US spot bitcoin ETFs took $191m of net inflow on Thursday 24 September, led by BlackRock's IBIT at $163m, extending a six-session streak worth $2.8bn - which includes $999m on Monday 22 September, the largest day of 2026, and about $347m on Wednesday 23 September with IBIT at roughly $166m and Fidelity's FBTC at $143m. September now stands at $2.56bn of net inflow against $3.52bn in August. The point for dip-buying is that regulated money kept adding on the exact day real yields spiked and BTC fell from $87,200 to $83,500, so the recent weakness was leverage unwinding, not distribution.

drivers.title: The year's largest options expiry cleared at 08:00 UTC and leverage is lighter than on Monday
drivers.detail: About 181,900 BTC of Deribit options worth roughly $14.4bn settled at 08:00 UTC today alongside some $1.8bn of ETH - 41.5% of bitcoin open interest and the largest expiry of the year - with a call-heavy put/call ratio of 0.69 and max pain between $72,000 and $76,000, far below spot. It passed without a break. Meanwhile Hyperliquid open interest has fallen across all three majors since the 22 September briefing (BTC $3.39bn from $4.02bn, ETH $2.96bn from $3.18bn, SOL $726m from $746m) with funding flat at 0.00125%/h and premiums of 0.019-0.084%. Positioning is lighter now than before this week's drawdown, which is the condition under which dips have historically been shallow.

drivers.title: Trump-Xi summit passes without incident; trade truce extended into January 2027
drivers.detail: Trump hosted Xi Jinping at the White House on 24 September and called it a 'very good meeting'. No comprehensive agreement was announced on tariffs, rare earths, soybeans, AI or Taiwan - Beijing's ambassador restated Taiwan as a red line - but the two sides extended the existing trade truce through January 2027, pushing out the 10 November Busan expiry. This removes the binary that had been the largest scheduled geopolitical risk of the week: the summit did not collapse over the pending $14bn Taiwan arms package.

drivers.title: CFTC keeps issuing crypto guidance while the CLARITY Act stays dead in the Senate
drivers.detail: The CFTC's Market Participants, Market Oversight and Clearing and Risk divisions released updated crypto FAQs on 24 September covering investment of customer funds in tokenized versions of permitted investments and the use of blockchain for registrant recordkeeping, building on Staff Letters 25-39 and 26-05, with Chairman Michael Selig framing it as ongoing regulatory clarity. That is the agency route, and it is all there is: the Senate's cloture vote on the Digital Asset Market Clarity Act failed 49-50 on 15 September against the 60 needed, leaving US market structure in limbo. Constructive at the margin, but no legislative catalyst is coming.

watch.what: Bitget's incident report deadline, and the first real test of whether withdrawals resume. A clean reopening closes the story; another delay is the one thing on today's board that could turn a contained hack into a confidence event across exchange balances.

The 10-year Treasury yield at 5.171% after touching 2007 highs on Wednesday. The pause is what is supporting risk right now; a retest of the highs is the cleanest path back to an $83,000 handle on BTC.

Solana's Alpenglow mainnet activation, the largest protocol change of the quarter and the main asset-specific risk among the three majors - SOL is also the most leveraged to it on the thinnest book at $726m of open interest.
US Consumer Confidence. Secondary, but it feeds the same real-yield channel that drove this week's drawdown.

BEA Personal Income and Outlays with the August PCE print (ADP 12:15 UTC, GDP third estimate 12:30 UTC), on quarter-end when flows get pulled around. The Fed's own 2026 projections are 3.7% headline and 3.4% core PCE with most participants signalling at least one more hike this year, so a hot print reopens the hike debate directly.
September employment report. First-Friday payrolls into a Fed that has already hiked once and is guiding for more.

Context for any pullback, from the stored history: BTC has had 28 sharp dips, with +1.5% recovered within 14 days in 92.9% of cases (median 5.0 h, 78.6% within 24 h) and a typical extra drop after the trigger of -0.5%; dips during greed recovered in 7 of 7 for BTC, 92.9% of 28 for ETH and 93.8% of 48 for SOL. Today's market state most resembles 2025-07-11, 2025-10-04 and 2024-07-21, after which BTC's median 30-day move was 8.0% (up in 60.0% of them). The one precursor to respect: 'Donald Trump (Truth Social) + inflation/CPI' preceded a BTC dip within 6h 2.6% of the time versus 1.0% by chance (2.72x lift, n=115).
